_meta.description: Defines the vocabulary this dashboard invents, alongside the industry terms it borrows. Our own scales are subjective judgments, not analyst ratings — they are defined here so they can be argued with.

terms.d: How strongly we hold the name. 1 = monitor, 2 = interested, 3 = high conviction. A subjective judgment by the author, not a rating. New names enter at 1-2; a 3 has to be argued for.

How far the equity has run ahead of the fundamental case. 1 = insulated (thesis not in the price), 2 = exposed, 3 = high froth (price embeds years of good news). Froth is about ENTRY PRICE, not business quality — a froth-3 name can be an excellent company.
An insulated (froth-1) name trading 15%+ below its 52-week high AND not up more than 60% over 12 months. The second condition matters: a 50% drawdown after a 10x run is profit-taking, not value.
How far through its structural cycle a vertical is. Innings 1-3 mean most of the return is still ahead but patience is required; 7-9 mean the thesis is largely priced.
How starved of investment the supply chain has been. Above 80 means a decade or more of under-investment, so supply cannot answer a price signal quickly.
How tightly earnings track GDP. Below 30 means demand is policy-driven or physically non-discretionary and survives a recession.
The mechanical instruction the Act Now page derives from our own conviction and froth tags: STAGE, STOP ADDING, BUY THE DISLOCATION, THESIS AT RISK, REVIEW or MONITOR.
Measured signals are computed from prices and are facts. Unverified signals are parsed from headlines — plausible, but not independently confirmed. The distinction is shown on every Act Now card.
A sector that consumes commodities rather than producing them (electricity and grid, energy infrastructure, digital infrastructure). It has no Dimension A column because it is not a commodity chain.
A step in a supply chain where a small number of suppliers can constrain everything downstream. REE separation and uranium enrichment are the clearest examples in this universe.
Producers ranked by cost per unit. Low-cost producers survive price troughs that close high-cost supply; position on the curve determines who is a forced seller.
The price required to justify building new supply. Spot below the incentive price means the deficit persists regardless of demand.
Contango = forward prices above spot (comfortable supply). Backwardation = spot above forward, which signals physical scarcity now.
A financing structure that buys future production at a fixed cost. Zero operating cost inflation and no capex, with full exposure to the commodity price.
Percentage below the 52-week high. Used here as an entry-timing input, never on its own — see entry window.
High-assay low-enriched uranium (5-20% U-235), required by most advanced reactor designs. Western commercial supply is close to zero.
Heavy rare earth elements (dysprosium, terbium and others). Scarcer than light REEs and almost entirely separated in China.
In-situ recovery: dissolving uranium underground and pumping it out. Cheaper and faster to restart than conventional mining.
Treatment and refining charges paid to smelters. Falling charges signal concentrate scarcity — a leading copper indicator.
